title: Cycle Capacity Prism: Prioritized Buffer, Skill-Swap Protocol, and Graceful Scope Fallthrough
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: As usage for Redwood Dedicated grows and cross-team dependencies increase, we lack a deterministic mechanism to (a) prioritize a small buffer of capacity across initiatives, (b) trigger skill-constrained staff swaps without disrupting domain work, and (c) fall through scope to safe, testable shims when headcount or blocker risk spikes.

Goal: Produce a concise, operational 'Capacity Prism' that visualizes per-initiative criticality across four orthogonal axes (user-impact, latency/cost risk, compliance/regulatory exposure, and release date constraint) and ties that to a: prioritized buffer ledger, a lightweight skill-swap protocol (shadow + handoff steps), and a guarded scope-fallthrough policy for mid-cycle de-scopes.

Why now: Q2 ramp for Private deployments + new SLA tiers means we will see frequently competing requests for limited senior infra/serving engineers. Current ad-hoc swaps cause rework and unclear ownership. This artifact will reduce mid-cycle firefights and enable predictable commitments for PMs and Eng.

Non-goals: Replacing hiring or changing long-term headcount plans; building automation to move people (that is an ops concern). We're defining a decision protocol and tooling placeholders (Google Sheets + a simple scriptable scoring CSV).

Scope: Deliver playbook doc, a templated Google Sheet (Capacity Prism scoring, buffer ledger), a minimal Slack workflow template for swap requests, and a one-pager for exec rollout + 2-week pilot with 3 initiatives (Console Observability, Dedicated Autoscaling, Private VPC onboarding).

decisions: D1: Compliance/regulatory exposure will be weighted higher by default (3x multiplier) for Private deployments and enterprise customers
D2: A prioritized buffer of 10% of allocated FTEs per cycle will be maintained as 'soft buffer' for high-risk initiatives; buffer can be consumed only via approved swap protocol
D3: Skill-swap protocol requires: (a) shadow period of 2 working days, (b) documented checklist attached to swap request, (c) stakeholder acknowledgement in Slack thread
D4: Graceful scope fallthrough rules: features flagged as 'non-blocker' go to a 'shim' or 'degraded mode' with test coverage retained; formal de-scopes must list rollback steps and monitoring metrics
